svg.title: Hub-and-Spoke Network
svg.desc: Hub-and-Spoke Network. Shared services and egress in a central hub network; workloads live in peered spokes. Step 1, Every network, own edge: Each network runs its own firewall, VPN, internet exit and DNS, and Prod and Data share one range. Step 2, A hub of shared services: One hub holds the shared firewall, gateway, DNS and bastion; each workload gets a peered spoke. Step 3, Traffic through the hub: Spokes route via the hub firewall: Prod reaches Data only through it; on-premises enters at the hub. Step 4, Grow, know the limits: A new spoke is a template plus one peering, but the hub has limits: throughput, quotas, cost per GB.

g.text: Each network runs its own firewall, VPN, internet exit and DNS, and Prod and Data share one range.
One hub holds the shared firewall, gateway, DNS and bastion; each workload gets a peered spoke.
Spokes route via the hub firewall: Prod reaches Data only through it; on-premises enters at the hub.
A new spoke is a template plus one peering, but the hub has limits: throughput, quotas, cost per GB.
Prod and Data both use 10.1.0.0/16, so they can't be peered without renumbering.
The platform team owns the hub: one firewall, one gateway, shared DNS, a bastion.
Each workload team owns its spoke, peered to the hub but not to the other spokes.
One address plan, nothing overlaps: Data is renumbered to 10.3.0.0/16.
every spoke: routes and DNS server
firewall log: one rule set for every spoke
